A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoED GNN research, with matching authors, architecture and core experiments. The main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CoED evaluations, synthetic lattice and gene-regulatory-network experiments, and regression results on Perturb-seq, web traffic and power-grid data, with experimental details in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds classification evaluations, runtime measurements, CIFAR-feature experiments and analyses of oversmoothing and learned edge directions.

M1.justification: The continuous phase parameters, fuzzy Laplacian, separate incoming/outgoing aggregation, self-feature transformation and joint optimization remain unchanged. Optional directional weighting and layer-specific angles already existed in v1. The new SC-GAT variant is a comparator, not a modification of CoED.

E1.justification: Classification coverage expands from five to eleven datasets, adding Roman-Empire, SNAP-Patents, Arxiv-Year, Citeseer, AM-Computers and AM-Photo. Appendix H also evaluates triangular-lattice regression with CIFAR-derived RGB features, introducing structured image inputs alongside the retained random-feature scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Chung and Cooperative GNN comparisons, and Table 2 adds Chung on both synthetic tasks. Appendix H compares against self-consistent GAT and Co-GNN. The evaluated DirGNN variants also expand: Texas and Wisconsin use DirSAGE in v2 rather than the GCN-based implementation selected in v1.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1 replaces original Squirrel and Chameleon data with filtered versions removing redundant nodes, broadens reported hyperparameter searches and changes selected configurations, including DirGNN convolution types. New runtime experiments fix three layers and 64 hidden dimensions while varying graph or batch size. Appendix H introduces RGB-feature and repeated-Laplacian-convolution evaluations.

E4.justification: New Appendices G–I examine runtime scaling and phase-learning overhead, test whether enforcing consistent GAT edge weights explains CoED's advantage, compare depth sensitivity with CIFAR features, measure Dirichlet-energy decay, and visualize learned Perturb-seq directions. The earlier synthetic direction-recovery and depth analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report classification means and standard deviations across ten splits and graph-ensemble summaries from the top five of seven differently initialized runs. v2 introduces no stated change to these practices, seed counts, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures. Additional error-bar plots do not establish a new uncertainty-estimation method.

E6.justification: Table 1 substantially expands and replaces results. CoED's Squirrel/Chameleon accuracies change from 75.32/79.69 to 45.50/47.27 under filtered data; these are not same-setting losses. DirGNN's Texas accuracy changes from 68.38 to 83.78 with a different configuration. Table 2 adds Chung losses of 8.03 and 62.95, both scaled by 10^-3. Existing Table 2 rows and Table 3 remain unchanged; Appendices G–I add timing and diagnostic findings.

T1.justification: Appendix F.1 corrects the Hermitian adjacency definition from S multiplied elementwise by the phase matrix to S multiplied elementwise by its complex exponential. The spectral properties and expressivity proofs otherwise remain substantively unchanged. Main-text Theorem 1 restates the existing Appendix E result.

C1.justification: The fuzzy-Laplacian, weak-WL expressivity and joint edge-direction-learning contributions are retained. v2 modestly narrows the performance claim by explicitly specifying graph-ensemble datasets in the abstract and qualifying applicability in the introduction with an overfitting warning for masked-node classification.

C2.justification: v2 adds a substantive explanation of overfitting when training and testing hold out different nodes, expands the argument for feature-independent directions in Appendix H, and interprets new runtime and Dirichlet-energy evidence. It adds an explanation of Chung's behavior and removes v1's explanation that DirGNN performs poorly on Texas/Wisconsin because it does not separately process self-features.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 substantially expands dataset provenance, split instructions, search details and selected configurations, replacing one combined classification hyperparameter table with Tables A.1–A.8. v2 adds Chung configurations, reports an additional 80GB A100 and approximately three weeks of classification training rather than five days, and documents new runtime and RGB-feature setups. The code repository is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Chung, Cooperative GNNs, historical magnetic-Laplacian references, magnetic eigenmaps, DIGRAC flow-imbalance clustering and additional benchmark sources. These broaden attribution and comparisons without replacing the existing research positioning. Publication updates for the Wu and Xu papers represent the same cited works.

P1.justification: There are targeted introduction and results rewrites, clearer strong/weak WL explanations, a more explicit Section 5.1 heading, a displayed main-text theorem and new acknowledgments. Appendices G–I extend the document, but the original section sequence and most existing exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 is redesigned for eleven datasets and additional methods; classification settings are reorganized into multiple tables. v2 adds two runtime tables and Figures H.1–H.4 and I.1, covering illustrative graphs, image-derived features, diagnostic curves and learned directions. Existing experimental plots and theory illustrations are retained, including illustrations with corrected numbering.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evaluation credibility through filtered benchmarks and broader DirGNN configurations, reducing an earlier apparent CoED advantage under restricted comparisons. New attention controls, oversmoothing measurements and runtime studies provide more direct evidence about the central mechanism and its computational cost. The explicit overfitting limitation better bounds applicability. Some new CIFAR and timing experiments remain incompletely specified for replication, but the gains in comparison quality, diagnostic evidence and transparency are substantial.
